summary: Checkpoint trimming yields writer and disk time between background chunks and advances exhaustion checks through indexed tombstones

replay.detail: The same recorded tombstones and graph checks govern deletion. Interrupted trims resume through the existing state.

schema.detail: No production schema or stored format changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint retention rules, proof terms or capability versions change.

compatibility.detail: Checkpoint identities and replication invalidation remain unchanged. Background chunks rest for max(100 ms, four times their writer hold including commit), capped at five seconds; large trims take longer to finish.

downtime.detail: No extra startup work or service interruption. Individual SQL steps and commits can still exceed the chunk budget.

manual.detail: No configuration or operator action is required.

recovery.detail: Tombstones precede deletion, graph-changing chunks roll back, and the existing final completion marker is retained.
